belief: I'm less valuable because of where I come from.
origins: Mockery of an accent, a neighborhood, or a country, or being treated as a representative of a stereotype, teaches us that our origin is a defect. Over time, we may apologize for it, hide it, or conclude it makes us less.
teaches: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Nathanael asked, and Philip answered, “Come and see.” Jesus Himself grew up in a despised town. Scripture says, “From one man He made every nation of men,” and that God “determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.” “The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.” We are each “fearfully and wonderfully made.” Our place of birth is part of our story, but it is not a measure of our worth.
self_statements: Where I come from is a disadvantage.
I should be ashamed of my background.
My accent marks me as lesser.
People from my place are worth less.
I have to hide my origin.
I started behind and will stay behind.
errors: Letting a place define my worth.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that my origin is shameful.
Focusing on disadvantages and missing strengths.
Assuming others look down on me.
questions: What was good about the place I come from?
Who taught me to be ashamed, and what did they gain?
What strengths did I gain from my origin?
What does Scripture say about nations and places?
How did Jesus’ hometown look to others?
How might I honor my origin and still grow?
truth: My worth comes from being made by God, not from my place of birth. My origin shaped me, and it is part of my story. I can tell it with honesty and dignity.
hw_truths: God made every nation from one man.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
Good can come from small places.
The Lord is Maker of us all.
My origin is part of my story.
I do not have to hide.
log: Each week, note one strength from your origin.
actions: Write five good things about where you come from.
Write who taught it and what is false.
Cook, visit, or call in a way that honors where you came from.
prayer: Father, You made me and placed me in my time and place. Free me from shame about where I come from, and help me honor it with dignity. Amen.
hw_questions: What was good about my origin?
How can I honor my roots?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God made every nation, and my origin is part of His design.”
